intro: Pine forest, sea and stone: welcome to Phaselis, an ancient city in Antalya province from the 7th century BC. This was a seaside port city with three natural harbours, ringed by pine forest.
history: Phaselis was founded by Rhodians, and it prospered on trade in rose oil and timber. It even hosted a famous guest: Alexander the Great spent a winter here.
structure-1: You are now in front of Hadrian's Gate. This triumphal-arch gateway was built in honour of the Roman emperor Hadrian. Imagine walking through it as he might have.
structure-5: Here are the Baths. These Roman baths had underfloor heating, with hot and cold rooms. Picture the steam, and the city's chatter echoing off these walls.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Main Street and the Theatre, and seek out the three harbours.
facts: Did you know? Phaselis had three harbours within walking distance of each other, so that whichever way the wind blew, one was sheltered. The ancient main street, a colonnaded street, still connects two of those harbours, and you can walk it. Alexander the Great wintered here in 333 BC, and the city greeted him with a golden crown. And its wealth? It grew rich on rose oil and timber.
outro: This brings our journey through Phaselis to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
